title: Finding the Area of Any Triangle
summary: Learn the sine area formula so you can find triangle areas, missing angles, and unknown side expressions confidently.

items.prompt: A triangle has sides 6 cm and 10 cm, with an included angle of $40°$. Which calculation gives its area?
items.explanation: Use $A=\frac{1}{2}ab\sin C$, where $C$ is the angle between sides $a$ and $b$. Therefore the calculation is $\frac{1}{2}\times 6\times 10\times \sin 40°$.

items.prompt: A triangle has sides 11 cm and 13 cm with an included angle of $40°$. What is its area to 1 decimal place?
A triangle has sides 10 cm and 16 cm and an area of $40\text{ cm}^2$. The included angle $x$ is obtuse. What is $x$?
items.explanation: $40=\frac{1}{2}\times 10\times 16\times \sin x$, so $\sin x=0.5$. The calculator gives $30°$, but the obtuse angle with the same sine is $180°-30°=150°$.

items.prompt: Two sides of a triangle meet at $30°$. Their lengths are in the ratio $4:3$, and the area is $96\text{ cm}^2$. What is the shorter side?
items.explanation: Write the sides as $4k$ and $3k$. Then $96=\frac{1}{2}(4k)(3k)\sin 30°=3k^2$, so $k=4\sqrt{2}$. The shorter side is $3k=12\sqrt{2}$ cm.

items.prompt: A triangle has area $54\text{ cm}^2$. Two sides enclosing an angle of $30°$ have lengths 9 cm and $x$ cm. Find $x$.
items.explanation: Using $A=\frac{1}{2}ab\sin C$ gives $54=\frac{1}{2}\times 9\times x\times \sin 30°=2.25x$. Therefore $x=54\div 2.25=24$ cm.
